description.narrative:
The post PROSELL project will be implemented in thirty (30) communities across three (3) LGAs building on and scaling up on the PROSELL project accomplishments. To ensure that the post implementation is building on PROSELL building blocks, defined criteria was set to be used to select 3 LGAs (Kurmi/central zone, Wukari/southern zone and Zing/northern zone) from the initial 6 LGAs for PROSELL to inform the post-PROSELL intervention. The criteria for selection include: - Number of self-managed VSLA group as at PROSELL close-out. - Percentage of women VSLA and none VSLA members involved in IGA activities. - Percentage repayment rate into the PROSELL inputs revolving funds scheme.
The target groups are farmers from vulnerable households with a priorityon women to strengthen their economic empowerment and access to finance. State and non-state actors with a focus on improved service delivery.
The post PROSELL project envisages gaps from the PROSELL project as reflected in the evaluation report whichdetailed: “The PROSELL project encountered significant challenges across various aspects, revealing inherent weaknesses. Bureaucratic hurdles were faced at critical levels, including NIRSAL, off-takers, financial institutions, and state and local government policy levels. These challenges adversely affectedthe project's effectiveness, notably impeding interventions that aimed to link farmers, off-takers, and financing institutions to an agricultural de-risking facility. The PROSELL project faced notableweaknesses, particularly in achieving training targets, which manifested as specific challenges.” These are the problems that the post PROSELL project will aim to address.
Opportunities for additional impact as detailed in the evaluation report will be derived from the gaps reported which includes:  53.67% of respondents reported struggling with limited financial literacy, emphasizing the project's shortfall in adequately addressing the economic management skills of its beneficiaries.  Economic shocks were recognized as a challenge by 16.51% of respondents, underscoring vulnerabilities to external pressures.  Bureaucratic delays at state and local government levels impacted the creation of a radio program, potentially compromising the communicationstrategy's effectiveness. Security challenges, ranging from arrests to ethnic clashes, were widespread across different LGAs. These statistics substantiate the weaknesses within the PROSELL project, highlighting the importance of targeted interventions for comprehensive and impactful community development in the post PROSELL phase.
In addressing these evaluation gaps and seizing the opportunities identified, the post-PROSELL project will expect to achieve comprehensive and impactful community development outcomes for improved services, including improved economic empowerment, enhanced resilience to shocks, increased productivity, and better access to essential services for vulnerable households, particularly women-headed households. This willinclude reviewing and revising strategies to address the specific challenges encountered in achieving targets under the previous project phase.
The post PROSELL project at the impact level will improve economic management skills among vulnerable households,enhance their resilience to external pressures, particularly during economic downturns, increase productivity and income for women-headedhouseholds, streamline bureaucratic processes for improved program efficiency and communication, address security challenges to ensure safety and continuity of operations and enhance the effectiveness of training interventions for sustainable agricultural practices, economic empowerment and improved social services.
To this end, the PROSELL activities will be continued at a downsized scale post-PROSELL 2024 with its focus being on deepening financial inclusion in market enterprise, strengthening existing systems for improved services and strengthening accountability platforms and mechanisms.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
